post.caption:
The Sun delivers more energy to Earth in an hour than humanity uses in a year, so supply was never the constraint. Cost was, and solar cost per watt has collapsed over two decades to the point where it is the cheapest new generation in most of the world. Which moves the argument downstream. Peak solar is midday, peak demand is evening, and the grid stores almost nothing. Storage, transmission and battery materials are where the real engineering fight now is.
